entities.name: depression-like behavior in myofascial pain syndrome rats

relationships.subject: PDGFR-α
relationships.evidence_quote: These results indicate that PDGFR-α induces neuroinflammation, altered autophagy, and depressive behavior, potentially mediated by the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway in MPS rats.

relationships.subject: PDGFR-α
relationships.object: depression-like behavior in myofascial pain syndrome rats
relationships.evidence_quote: Treatment with inhibitors of PDGFR-α or JAK2/STAT3 alleviated depressive behaviors

relationships.subject: PDGFR-α
relationships.evidence_quote: increased the protein levels of BDNF and 5HT1AR

key_findings: PDGFR-α phosphorylation, inflammatory factors and p-JAK2/p-STAT3 are upregulated in the hippocampus of MPS rats with depression-like behavior.
Inhibiting PDGFR-α or JAK2/STAT3 alleviated depressive behaviors, raised BDNF and restored autophagy.
